amounts of goods and services equal to those of the private sector

questions.questionText: Which of the effects of economic development is an external cost?
What is likely to decrease the level of saving in an economy?

options.text: an increase in the general level of income
an increase in the number of cheap offers in shops
a redistribution of income from poor to rich households
a rise in the rate of interest

questions.questionText:
Which change will make a manufacturing company replace machines with labour to maintain the
most efficient combination of factors of production?

options.text: The price of the product manufactured has increased.
The productivity of labour has increased.
The productivity of machinery has increased.
The wages of labour have increased.

questions.questionText:
Although there are higher paid jobs in offices many workers stay in low-paid jobs on farms.
What might explain this in developing economies?

options.text: Agricultural workers lack the necessary education and skills.
Governments plan to increase indirect taxes on services.
Manual workers are being replaced by machines.
Workers on farms have high labour mobility.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows two curves. One is the demand for labour, the other is the supply of labour. A
government fixes a minimum wage (M ) that must be paid by employers.

labour employed
What will be the effect of this minimum wage?

options.text: no change in the market equilibrium
no worker will be paid wage W
supply of labour will exceed demand

questions.questionText: Which is an internal diseconomy of scale?

options.text: a lack of communication in a firm
a reduction of cost by buying in bulk
a shortage of skilled labour in an area
traffic congestion in a particular area

questions.questionText: What distinguishes a multinational company from other types of company?

options.text: It produces outside its country of origin.
It promotes its products in trade fairs abroad.

questions.questionText:
A major computer company announced that its profits had fallen below the level predicted.
What might have caused this?

options.text: increased advertising costs that greatly improved sales
low prices that made the company’s product competitive

Why is the Human Development Index (HDI) often considered to be better than Gross Domestic
Product (GDP) per head as a measure of living standards?

options.text: GDP per head excludes economic growth.
GDP per head ignores population growth.
HDI includes more than the production of goods and services.
HDI is calculated by the national government.

questions.questionText:
A finance minister reported that the economy was experiencing inflation and economic growth.
What would be evidence that both of these had occurred?

options.text: increased imports and increased income tax
increased interest rates and increased net migration

questions.questionText:
What would be a cause of cost-push inflationary pressure in an industry which supplies mobile
(cell) phones?

options.text: an increase in advertising expenses for mobile phones
an increase in export duties on mobile phones
an increase in income taxes on wages of employees
an increase in world demand for mobile phones

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause an increase in the population growth of a developing country?

options.text: a decrease in the birth rate
a decrease in the death rate
a decrease in the standard of living

questions.questionText:
At the start of the year a developing country had a population of 1000000, its birth rate was 16.0
per thousand per annum and its death rate was 8.0 per thousand per annum. At the end of the
year the population was 1005000.
What could explain this change in the population?
What is a benefit of tariffs?
Which name is given to the external value of a currency in terms of another currency?

It was reported in 2011 that the United States (US) needed to achieve a lower current account
deficit.
What would help this in the short run?

options.text: investment in the US by multinational firms
